note: VPcmV34GetVisualDiagnostics against t_v34diag.  Nine selectors that store the same output array from four different sources each, so every anchor is widened with the neighbouring statement that names the arm -- finding F347's remedy.  The two `maxCount` mutations on selectors 3 and 4 are the ones that adjudicate D710: they make the function HONOUR the bound, which is the fix the object does not have, and the suite has to catch that as a difference.

label: selector 0: the V.34 ring is not drained

label: selector 0: the ring count is not clamped
selector 0: the ring count is read unsigned
find: n = (unsigned int)obj->hist1_idx;
why: An argument about the code and not about the grid: the two readings are the SAME FUNCTION over every defined execution.  They can only differ when `hist1_idx` is negative, and then the signed read gives 0xffffffff and the unsigned one 0x0000ffff -- so they differ only where `maxCount` exceeds 65535 and the loop is already walking `hist_2aa8`, which has 300 entries.  Every input that separates them is one where the unmutated function is reading tens of thousands of elements past the end of that array, so there is no defined execution on which the mutation changes an observable.  The signedness stands on `movswl 0x2aa4` at 0x72ec, which is forced; this entry records that nothing behavioural can confirm it.

if ((unsigned int)(obj->status - 1) > 1u &&
		    obj->status == V34DIAG_STATUS_K56FLEX &&
		    obj->role == VDIAG_ROLE_CALL)
why: Every K56flex member this function calls is a three-byte stub -- `xor %eax,%eax; ret` -- so `getDecisionErrors` returns 0 and writes nothing whatever the role is, and the arm's only other outcome is the 0 it starts with. The role test on this arm is therefore invisible in the OBJECT and not merely untested here.  It is the object's test all the same and is reproduced; the day the class gains a body this becomes a real mutation and this entry will start failing, which is the alarm it exists to raise.
